put.description: Whole-graph write: each step config is validated against its type — an unknown key, or a value of the wrong shape, is refused rather than stored, so a step the worker cannot read never reaches the database. Steps are upserted by id (carry the id from GET /sequences/{id}/steps to update a step in place; omit it to create one), edges are replaced wholesale. The graph is validated with the same rules activation enforces, so a shape that could not activate is refused here with the same error keys. Steps that contacts have already passed through are permanent history and cannot be deleted. Removing a true/false branch edge that a CONDITION step had before the write is refused unless allowBranchRemoval is true — a one-branch condition is valid ("stop here"), so the loss would otherwise be silent. Only DRAFT and PAUSED sequences can be edited; pause an active sequence first. Pass expectedUpdatedAt to fail with 409 instead of overwriting a concurrent edit. The 200 response includes a diff of what the write changed (steps created/updated/deleted, edges added/removed).

info.title: SendHeron API
info.description:
Public REST API for managing contacts, tags, sequences, templates, suppressions, and email sending.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a Bearer token (API key) in the `Authorization` header.
Generate API keys from the dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

## Rate Limiting
Two one-minute ceilings apply to every request: a per-key limit, and a per-organization limit split by READ / WRITE / SEND so that reads cannot exhaust the sending budget. There is no hourly or daily quota — the multi-window throttler applies to the GraphQL dashboard API, not to this one.
Responses include `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` also carries `Retry-After`, and its headers name the ceiling (per-key, per-route or per-organization) that refused the request. A `429` never consumes an idempotency key. Current ceilings are readable at `GET /api/v1/usage`.

## Send outcomes
A `201` from a send route is an outcome, not proof of dispatch: `status` is `sent`, or `suppressed` with the machine-readable block reason in `errorMessage` (never retry those). Provider failures are `503` with the FAILED attempt recorded — retry with the same idempotency key. Anything else 4xx is a request bug.

## Scopes
API keys are scoped to specific permissions. Every scope an endpoint lists is required, and they are not alternatives. Available scopes: `contacts:read`, `contacts:write`, `sequences:read`, `sequences:write`, `templates:read`, `templates:write`, `analytics:read`, `emails:send`, `suppressions:read`, `suppressions:write`, `sending:read`, `sending:write`.

bearer.description: API key from Settings > API Keys

tagIds.description: Tag UUIDs to assign to the contact

tagNames.description: Tag names to assign (auto-created if they do not exist)

email.description: Contact email — used as the unique key for deduplication

properties.description: Custom properties (JSONB). Merged with existing on update.

status.description: BOUNCED/UNSUBSCRIBED/COMPLAINED cannot be overwritten to SUBSCRIBED

tagIds.description: Tag UUIDs to add to the contact (merged with existing tags). Alternative: use tagNames.

tagNames.description: Tag names to add (auto-created if not found). Alternative to tagIds.

removeTagNames.description: Tag names to remove from the contact (e.g. clearing superseded lifecycle tags). Never auto-created; a no-op if the contact lacks them.

properties.description: Custom properties as key-value pairs (merged with existing)

status.description: Contact subscription status. BOUNCED/UNSUBSCRIBED/COMPLAINED cannot be set to SUBSCRIBED

tagIds.description: Tag UUIDs to add. Provide tagIds, tagNames, or both.

tagNames.description: Tag names to add (auto-created if not found). Provide tagIds, tagNames, or both.

ref.description: Client-local reference for this step, used by edges. Any short string, unique within the payload.

id.description: Existing step UUID to update in place. Omit to create a new step. Steps that contacts have already passed through cannot be deleted, so repairs should carry existing ids.

config.description:
Step configuration. The keys depend on `type`, and a key this step type does not read is REJECTED rather than stored — a config the worker cannot understand used to be accepted silently and simply never run.

TRIGGER: `triggerType` (manual | contact_created | list_added | tag_added | event | webhook), plus `tagId` (UUID) for tag_added, `listId` (UUID) for list_added, `eventName` for event, and an optional `source` filter for contact_created.
SEND_EMAIL: `templateId` (UUID).
DELAY: `duration` (positive number) and `unit` (minutes | hours | days). A delay of one week is `{"duration": 168, "unit": "hours"}` or `{"duration": 7, "unit": "days"}` — there is no `days` key.
CONDITION: `field`, `operator`, and `value` where the operator takes one.
ACTION: `actionType`, plus `tagId` or `tagName` for tag actions, `properties` for property updates, `webhookUrl` (https) for webhooks.

Values are validated here; whether a step is COMPLETE is checked at activation, so a draft may still omit required keys.

fromRef.description: Ref of the step this edge leaves.

toRef.description: Ref of the step this edge enters.

edgeType.description: default for linear flow; true/false only from CONDITION steps.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Optimistic concurrency guard: the sequence's updatedAt you last read. A mismatch returns 409 instead of silently overwriting someone else's edit.

allowBranchRemoval.description: Confirm removing a true/false branch edge that a CONDITION step had before this write. Without it such a payload is refused (400 branchRemovalNeedsConfirmation): a one-branch condition is a valid graph ("stop here"), so the dropped branch would otherwise take effect silently — contacts taking that outcome just stop. Retargeting a branch (same edgeType, different destination) needs no flag.

status.description: ACTIVE resumes the sequence, and is refused unless the graph is sound: at least one step, a trigger, no orphans, and every step configured well enough to run. PAUSED stops contacts advancing while keeping their position, so resuming continues rather than restarts.

contactIds.description: Array of contact UUIDs to enroll
Array of contact UUIDs whose enrollments to cancel

content.description: File content, base64-encoded. Bytes are passed straight to the provider and never stored. Deliberately excluded from the idempotency fingerprint: a retried job that regenerates the file (a fresh creation timestamp inside the PDF) replays the original response instead of failing the key with 409.

type.description: MIME type. Only allowlisted types are accepted.

disposition.description: Only "attachment" is supported. Present for SendGrid payload compatibility; inline (CID) images are not supported.

from.description: Sender email address (defaults to org configured sender)

fromName.description: Display name for this send, overriding the sender identity's. The address is what domain verification gates; the name may vary per send (one verified address, several product names). No CR/LF or angle brackets.

cc.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Each address is checked against the suppression list independently — a cc is a real delivery.

headers.description: Custom headers. Headers the platform owns (List-Unsubscribe, authentication, envelope) are rejected rather than dropped.

sendAt.description: Schedule the send for a future time (ISO-8601). Cancel before it fires with DELETE /api/v1/emails/scheduled/{id}. Compliance is evaluated when it fires, not when it is scheduled.

attachments.description: Attachments (max 10, 10 MB decoded total, allowlisted MIME types). Transactional sends only — this route always qualifies. Not combinable with sendAt. Bytes are never stored, and are excluded from the idempotency fingerprint.

templateId.description: Template ID (UUID) to render and send

variables.description: Dynamic variables to render into the template (Handlebars/Liquid syntax). If contactId is provided, contact.* variables are auto-populated and merged with these.

contactId.description: Contact ID (UUID). When provided, auto-populates contact.* template variables (firstName, lastName, email, properties) and guarantees unsubscribe headers.

subject.description: Override the template subject line. Supports Handlebars/Liquid syntax with the same variables.

from.description: Sender email address (defaults to org configured sender)

fromName.description: Display name for this send, overriding the sender identity's. The address is what domain verification gates; the name may vary per send. No CR/LF or angle brackets.

cc.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Each address is checked against the suppression list independently — a cc is a real delivery, and a blocked copy is dropped without failing the message.

sendAt.description: Schedule the send for a future time (ISO-8601). The template is rendered and compliance is evaluated when it fires, not when it is scheduled. Cancel before it fires with DELETE /api/v1/emails/scheduled/{id}.

attachments.description: Attachments (max 10, 10 MB decoded total, allowlisted MIME types). Only allowed when the template is TRANSACTIONAL. Not combinable with sendAt. Bytes are never stored, and are excluded from the idempotency fingerprint.

templateId.description: UUID of the email template to use

from.description: Sender email address (defaults to org configured sender)

sampleData.description: Sample data for template variable previewing

listId.description: UUID of a list to send to (all contacts in the list)

contactIds.description: Specific contact UUIDs to send to

sendToAll.description: Send to all contacts in the organization

name.description: Tag name (must be unique per organization)

document.description: The block document to check. Returns the issues that would refuse it, empty when it would save.

bodyHtml.description: Raw HTML to preview. Supply exactly one of bodyHtml or document.

document.description: Block document to compile and preview. Schema: docs/template-document.md.

emailType.description: Template type to preview as. Decides whether the preview carries an unsubscribe block.

channel.description: Channel to preview through. A channel can only tighten the policy, never loosen it: CAMPAIGN and BULK are always marketing whatever the template says, so previewing through one shows the unsubscribe block a TRANSACTIONAL template would still gain.

sampleData.description: Values for the Handlebars variables, so the preview renders with real-looking content instead of empty placeholders.

bodyHtml.description: HTML body, for a raw-HTML template (supports Handlebars variables). Supply exactly one of bodyHtml or document — sending both is refused rather than one silently winning.

document.description: Block document, for a builder template. The server validates it and compiles bodyHtml from it, so the compiled HTML is always exactly what the blocks say — you cannot send bodyHtml alongside it. Schema and block reference: docs/template-document.md. Validate one without saving via POST /api/v1/templates/validate.

emailType.description: Email type. Required — the type decides suppression behavior and unsubscribe handling, so it must be declared, never defaulted: a password-reset template that silently became MARKETING would be blocked for exactly the users who unsubscribed and most need it.

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to associate with this template

document.description: Block document. An object recompiles the template from it, entering or staying in builder mode. An explicit null EJECTS to raw HTML: the document is dropped and the last compiled bodyHtml becomes editable. Omitting the field leaves the mode alone — and editing bodyHtml directly on a builder template is refused until it is ejected, so the blocks and the HTML can never disagree.

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to associate (replaces existing tags)

confirmEmailTypeChange.description: Required whenever emailType actually changes. Reclassifying a template is a compliance event — TRANSACTIONAL to MARKETING makes its sends consent-suppressible, the reverse strips unsubscribe handling — so a type change without this flag returns 400 (templates.emailTypeChangeNeedsConfirmation).

reason.description: Manual suppression reasons only. Bounce and complaint are recorded by the platform from provider events and cannot be set through this endpoint — accepting them would let a caller fabricate a deliverability record that blocks transactional mail.

note.description: Why this address is being suppressed. Shown to support.

confirmHardTier.description: Required to lift a bounce or complaint suppression. Those are deliverability facts, not preferences — re-mailing the address risks the sending domain, so it takes a deliberate acknowledgement.

note.description: Why this suppression is being lifted.

domain.description: The domain to authenticate, without scheme or path. Case and a trailing dot are normalized away. Authenticating a domain covers every address under it, including subdomains.

label.description: Human label shown when picking a sender.

fromEmail.description: The From address. Accepted whatever its domain, and reported as unsendable until that domain is authenticated in this workspace — so an identity can be prepared before the DNS is in place.

fromName.description: Display name recipients see beside the address.

replyToEmail.description: Where replies go, when that differs from the From address. Its domain does not have to be authenticated.
